name: THE CREEK & SLUICE
materialIdentity: The creek in the diggings, the community sluice on its far bank, one willow; night, the town's hour (errata 98, 99)
note: Room 26, doc 20: the creek and the community sluice, below the road to the claims (errata 99 A).

LOOK_AT.say: Quicksilver in an iron flask, chained to the sluice like the judges' pencil, and for the same reason.
repeat: The chain is newer than the flask. Somebody learned something.
It is heavier than it looks. It is the only thing out here that is.
A shift inside, slow and heavy, like something turning over in bed.
Nothing, until the chain moves, and then the slosh again, offended on principle.

overrides.OPEN: Chained, stoppered, and right. Quicksilver in this town would end up in the whiskey inside a week, as medicine.

LOOK_AT.say: A gold pan, in the willows, thrown. Not dropped. Thrown.
repeat: The bottom is worn bright from swirling. Whoever threw it had used it a long time first.
Nobody has picked it up. Out here a thrown pan is a kind of grave.
Water ticking against its rim in the shallows.
Nothing. It has been let go.

LOOK_AT.say: The cross-bars that are supposed to catch the gold. They catch sand, mercury beads, buttons, and once — the story goes — a wedding ring nobody would afterward claim.
repeat: Cleats to catch the heavy material. There is a great deal of heavy material and none of it is gold.
A brass button is caught on the third bar, with an anchor on it. A sailor came a very long way to lose it here.

LISTEN_TO.say: Grit, ticking along the bars. The sound of almost.
repeat: Nothing.
Grit, then nothing, then grit. It is catching its breath.

LOOK_AT.say: A man, crouched, doing the same motion he was doing when I passed this morning.
repeat: Swirl, tip, look, sigh, scoop. He has done it so long his shoulders have learned it without him.
He looked up at me once. He did not seem to see a person, only something that was not gold.

LISTEN_TO.say: Water, and breathing, and nothing else at all. He has not spoken in nine hours.
repeat: The pan's rim on stone, over and over, in perfect time. He would make a decent metronome.
Something very small under his breath: a tune with no middle to it, the same eight notes again.

LOOK_AT.say: The gate that feeds the sluice. Opening it is a privilege rotated weekly by a schedule everyone disputes and everyone obeys.
repeat: The schedule is nailed to the post beside it and amended in five hands. Two of the amendments are threats.
It leaks at the bottom. The creek gets through a little every day, on nobody's schedule.

LISTEN_TO.say: The creek, leaning on the boards. It would like to come through now, please.
repeat: Water pressing, polite and enormous.
A trickle at the bottom boards. The creek is not waiting for its week.

overrides.PULL: It is not my week. The schedule is disputed hourly and enforced absolutely.

LOOK_AT.say: The far bank, close enough to hit with a stone and claimed by a different set of men, who look exactly like this set.
repeat: They are working the same water a few feet over. A different claim and the same creek; that is the whole law of the district.
A man on the far side raised his hat to me. I raised mine. We have now met, and neither of us will mention it again.

LISTEN_TO.say: The same water, telling them the same thing.
repeat: Picks on the far side, a beat behind ours, like an echo with ambitions.
Someone over there laughing. It carries well across water, and it sounds expensive.

LOOK_AT.say: A community sluice, forty feet of graded boxes, patched by every man who ever cursed it.
repeat: Every patch is a different wood, and one patch is a door, with its number still on it.
The boxes are graded, the top ones wide and the bottom ones fine, so that what one man misses the next man misses more carefully.
then: It belongs to everyone, which means the repairs belong to no one.

LISTEN_TO.say: Water working through the riffles. A wooden argument, well rehearsed.
repeat: Water, through wood, forty times over. It's almost a chord. It is not quite a chord.
One box knocks out of time with the others. I could find which in a minute. Nobody has asked me.

overrides.PUSH: Forty feet of communal grievance, and every patch in it is somebody's signature. It does not move for one man. That is nearly the town motto.

LOOK_AT.say: One willow, spared by every axe because it holds the bank together.
repeat: Twenty or thirty sets of initials are cut into the trunk, and not one of them inside a heart. Out here people commit to nothing but their names.
It leans over the water as though it were panning too, and having about the same luck.
then: The only resident of the diggings with guaranteed tenure.

LISTEN_TO.say: Leaves. The single softest sound for a mile.
repeat: Leaves again. Softer than the water, softer than the men. The willow wins.
A bird somewhere inside it, saying one note and stopping, like a man who has thought better of it.

overrides.TALK_TO: The one resident with tenure. I paid my respects. It rustled: noted.

LOOK_AT.say: The creek that talked a thousand men into staying.
repeat: Six feet across and eight inches deep, and the reason two thousand people live here.
I followed it a little way upstream. It goes on being the same creek, which is more than most things here manage.
then: It carries just enough color to be cruel.

LISTEN_TO.say: Water over stone, saying the same encouraging thing it has said for twelve years.
repeat: Water. It is the only thing in this territory that is doing exactly what it appears to be doing.
Water, and under it the clink of a pan on stone a long way down.

overrides.USE: I panned twice. Color both times — four flakes, a day's wage in encouragement, a cent in gold. The creek's whole business model, in one pan.

LOOK_AT.say: The bank is a plaster cast of every boot in the district, refreshed daily.
repeat: Hobnailed, patched, and one barefoot. That man has my sympathy and my attention.
Mine are among them now. I've been counted.

LISTEN_TO.say: Mud, drying. The morning shift, set in relief.
repeat: Water seeping into the newest prints, filling them one at a time.
Nothing. Tomorrow's shift will print over today's, and nobody will be counted twice.
